LESSON: READING 8.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION: VISUALS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we say a picture is worth a thousand words?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify information from visuals for information
2. appreciate the role of summarising using visuals for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 8.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION: VISUALS
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 8.2.1 READING FOR INFORMATION: VISUALS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify information from visuals for information

What this means
In this part you learn to identify information from visuals for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify information from visuals for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify information from visuals for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the role of summarising using visuals for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of summarising using visuals for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of summarising using visuals for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of summarising using visuals for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify information from visuals for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals to a partner. (skill: appreciate the role of summarising using visuals for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify information from visuals for information.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of summarising using visuals for effective communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we say a picture is worth a thousand words?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 8.2.1 Reading for Information: Visuals means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify information from visuals for information.
5. Be able to: appreciate the role of summarising using visuals for effective communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
